description: Policy input for tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-firewall.sh. The tool renders the per-interface and per-app rules from this file, checks them with 'nft -c', and applies them atomically. Nothing here is applied by itself.

kernel_posture.per_app_match_note: nftables 'socket cgroupv2' matching needs Linux >= 5.13 and is NOT usable on this device. The loader selects nuxel-app-firewall.nft (classid) vs nuxel-app-firewall-cgroupv2.nft (VM/future) from the measured kernel.
kernel_posture.classid_derivation: classid = cgroup_classid from configs/nuxel/app-registry/app_registry.json when present, else 0x01030000 | (crc32(app_id) % 0xFFFD + 1) - identical to nuxel-permd.py _classid_for()

console_protection.reason: The live root console (CDC-ACM /dev/ttyGS0) is the only recovery path; the mission forbids flashing, so the console path must survive any firewall mistake. Network rules are also reverted automatically if an apply is not confirmed within rollback_seconds.

rollback.confirm_note: apply --rollback-after N arms a timer; run 'nuxel-firewall.sh confirm' (or the console stays reachable and the timer restores the previous ruleset).

usb0.note: USB gadget networking - owner console path

rndis0.note: USB RNDIS gadget - alias sometimes used by the host side

wlan0.note: Wi-Fi station interface; app traffic still requires a classid ACCEPT rule

rmnet0.note: cellular data; no modem bring-up on the S10+ yet, so it is explicitly disabled rather than silently assumed

tun0.note: VPN tunnel; only used with the kill switch armed

apps._comment: Per-app override of the classid ACCEPT rule. 'auto' = use the app registry's network_class (public -> allow, isolated -> drop). Keys are app_ids.

always_capture: nft -a list chain inet nuxel_app_firewall output
evidence.note: The tool prints the real 'nft list ruleset' output after every apply and stores it under /var/lib/nuxel/firewall/evidence/. A rule that cannot be shown in that output is not claimed as enforced.
